## 1. New LLM Versions / Major AI Lab Tools
- **2026-06-04 — [OpenAI: ChatGPT memory “Dreaming”](https://openai.com/index/chatgpt-memory-dreaming).** OpenAI introduced a new memory system intended to keep user preferences and recurring context fresher across conversations. **Why it matters:** Personalization is moving from session-level context toward persistent user-state management, raising both usefulness and governance stakes.

- **2026-06-04 — [OpenAI frontier models and Codex on AWS](https://openai.com/index/openai-frontier-models-and-codex-are-now-available-on-aws/).** OpenAI said its frontier models and Codex are available through AWS. **Why it matters:** This reduces enterprise adoption friction for AWS-standardized buyers and pushes OpenAI deeper into managed cloud procurement channels.

- **2026-06-04 — [OpenAI: GPT-Rosalind capabilities](https://openai.com/index/introducing-new-capabilities-to-gpt-rosalind/).** OpenAI introduced new GPT-Rosalind capabilities for enterprise life-sciences research, including stronger drug-discovery domain performance and GPT-5.5-linked tool use/coding behavior. **Why it matters:** Vertical frontier models are becoming more operational, not just advisory, in regulated R&D workflows.

- **2026-06-03 — [Google Labs: Dreambeans](https://blog.google/innovation-and-ai/models-and-research/google-labs/dreambeans/).** Google Labs introduced Dreambeans, a mobile experiment using personal context across Google services to generate a finite daily set of AI stories. **Why it matters:** Google is testing consumer personal-AI products that combine memory, cross-service context, and generated media.
